claims_audit.c2_finding: MAJOR taxonomy errors in C1 report narrative table (Rows 5, 8, 9, 10) and MAJOR error in ledger_v1 Claim 11; data layer (manifest_v3) uses correct canonical taxonomy throughout
claims_audit.evidence_source: ops01_taxonomy_v1.json vs PHASE_8_P2_R2_C1_CORRECTIVE_SUFFICIENCY_AUDIT_20260913.md table and ops01_corrective_audit_ledger_v1.json Claim 11
claims_audit.scope: ops01_taxonomy_v1.json canonical class names and abbreviations
claims_audit.discrepancy: C1 report table: (1) Row 5: MCC labeled Microalgae Bloom / Marine Organisms; canonical=Mesoscale Cellular Convection. (2) Row 8: OF labeled Oil Slick Lookalike / Organic Film; canonical=Ocean Front. (3) Row 9: POW labeled Rain Cell / Precipitation; canonical=Pure Ocean Wave. (4) Row 10: RF labeled Rain Cell Front; canonical=Rain Cell / Rain Footprint. Ledger_v1 Claim 11: OF class_id written as Class 8 (should be Class 6) and scope as Oil Slick lookalike (should be Ocean Front).
claims_audit.resolution: Data layer (manifest_v3 class_composition) uses correct abbreviations and class_names throughout. C1 report table errors are narrative-layer only. Ledger v2 (this document) corrects Claim 11. C2 report uses strictly canonical terminology.

claims_audit.c2_finding: C2 confirms: 5 distinct non-duplicate ocean basin labels extracted from Level-1 S3 annotation XML tiepoints for all 27 parents. Basin labels in manifest_v3: (1) Indo-Pacific / South China Sea / Indonesian Waters: 10 parents, (2) Indian Ocean / Arabian Sea / Bay of Bengal: 5 parents, (3) Mediterranean Sea: 3 parents, (4) South Atlantic Ocean: 1 parent, (5) Global Oceanic Waters: 8 parents. DISCREPANCY: C1 report table used Andaman Sea for basin 2 label but manifest_v3 uses Arabian Sea / Bay of Bengal. Minor label inconsistency.
claims_audit.evidence_source: geographic_location.ocean_basin field in ops01_physical_dataset_manifest_v3.json for all 27 parent scenes
claims_audit.discrepancy: C1 report table used Indian Ocean / Andaman Sea / Bay of Bengal for basin 2; manifest_v3 records Indian Ocean / Arabian Sea / Bay of Bengal. Geographic claim of 5 basins is supported by evidence from XML tiepoints. OVERCLAIM RISK: Global Oceanic Waters basin label is not a specific named ocean basin; it represents a catch-all label for North Sea, Coral Sea, and Beaufort Sea scenes. This does NOT constitute overclaim since the specific sub-basin names are documented in the C1 table.
claims_audit.resolution: The 5-basin claim is EVIDENCED (not merely asserted) via XML tiepoint extraction. The label Global Oceanic Waters is bounded by specific coordinates and sub-basin names in C1 table. No overclaim prohibited by evidence-boundary rules. C2 manifest_v3 basin labels are authoritative.

claims_audit.c1_reported_value: 0 duplicate sample IDs, 0 duplicate image hashes
claims_audit.c2_finding: 3 groups of samples share identical mask SHA256 hashes (7, 8, and 2 samples per group). All image SHA256 hashes are unique across all 147 samples. Mask duplicates are expected physics artifacts: crops covering the same single-class region produce identical mask PNGs (e.g., 100% MCC fraction = constant pixel value PNG). No duplicate sample IDs. No duplicate images.
claims_audit.evidence_source: SHA-256 content hashes of all 147 mask PNG files via manifest_v3
claims_audit.scope: Mask file content hashes (not sample IDs or image hashes)
claims_audit.discrepancy: None; duplicate mask hashes are structurally expected and do not constitute dataset contamination
claims_audit.resolution: Mask hash duplicates occur only when a crop window contains 100% of a single class label, producing a constant-value PNG that is hash-identical across different images from the same or different parents. Image hashes are all distinct; no sample duplication.
